data.description:
The Gerrit review bot fetches the tree from webhook-supplied `patchSet.ref` (`voter.py:366,374` →
`gerrit_client.py:368`) but casts its vote against `patchSet.revision` (`voter.py:657`). Those are
two independently-supplied fields, so the tree that was reviewed and the revision the vote attaches
to need not be the same commit — on one of the two mandatory merge gates.

Verified during approval and deliberately reframed: this is NOT a live vulnerability. Gerrit always
emits the pair consistently (each patchset has its own immutable `refs/changes/NN/CCCC/P`), so a
contributor cannot decouple them. Decoupling requires forging a webhook, which requires
`WEBHOOK_TOKEN` (`app.py:280`, correctly compared with `hmac.compare_digest`).

The durable justification is non-adversarial: `clone_change_ref` fetches into `repo_root`, and the
reviewed tree is whatever ends up there. A stale or reused clone dir, a partial fetch, or a future
refactor of the checkout logic all produce a tree that is not the voted revision, with no signal.

Scope refined by the maintainer to the assertion only. The `--end-of-options` hardening was dropped:
HTTPS transport already blocks the exploit path, and both proposers had independently scoped the
other ~89 git call sites out as a separate sweep.

`review_bot/adapter.py:184` takes `ref` as a required positional and never reads it. Both proposers
independently chose to give it this job rather than delete it, preserving the seam contract that
`adapter.py:6`, ADR 0009, ADR 0015, and `docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md:411-413` all describe.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] After fetch and checkout, the resolved `FETCH_HEAD` is asserted equal to `patchSet.revision`
- [ ] A mismatch refuses to vote, fail-closed, with an actionable message
- [ ] `adapter.py`'s `ref` parameter performs that assertion instead of being unread
- [ ] A test covers the mismatch path (a false mismatch would block all reviews)
data.title: Bind the reviewed tree to the voted revision in the review bot
